articles.title: Police Respond Quickly to Serious Incident on Ramsey Street
articles.excerpt: Police attended a serious incident on Ramsey Street in Rochdale quickly, with an officer providing medical care at the scene.
articles.content_html:
A serious incident occurred on Ramsey Street in Rochdale on 28 July 2026, prompting a swift response from local police. Officers arrived at the scene promptly and provided immediate assistance.

Witnesses reported seeing an officer delivering medical care, which was noted as a commendable action during the incident. The rapid response of the police has been acknowledged positively by members of the community.

Details regarding the nature of the incident have not been disclosed, and police have not released further information.

articles.title: Man jailed for taking weapons to Heywood school
articles.excerpt: A man has been sentenced to two years in prison after taking a hammer, hatchet and kitchen knife to a school in Heywood, claiming he wanted to create a scene for attention.
articles.content_html:
A man has been sentenced to two years in prison after taking a hammer, a hatchet and a kitchen knife to a school in Heywood. Both Douk Deng, 21, a South Sudanese national, was jailed at Manchester Minshull Street Crown Court for his actions on August 6 last year.

Deng became increasingly frustrated with immigration authorities, having applied for and been refused asylum on three occasions. He intended to create a scene for attention to aid his cause, the court heard.

He was arrested after workmen confronted him at Edgar Wood Academy, which was closed to pupils for the summer. A member of the public had alerted the authorities after seeing Deng behaving oddly in the street nearby, carrying a petrol can with a hammer tied to his belt.

Deng was observed walking a full circuit around the school, mumbling to himself, before builders on site called the police due to their concerns.

articles.title: Three men sentenced for running Rochdale's 'Adam Line' drug operation
articles.excerpt: Three men have been sentenced for their roles in a Rochdale drug line that generated over £1 million a year, despite previous police efforts to dismantle it.
articles.content_html:
Three men have been sentenced for their involvement in a drug line in Rochdale known as the 'Adam Line', which reportedly generated over £1 million a year. The operation continued despite multiple police interventions aimed at shutting it down.

Haider Ali, 34, known as 'The Ghost', was identified as the controller of the drug line. He was arrested after police observed a suspected drug deal on Baron Street. Officers found £1,000 in cash and wraps of cocaine and heroin on him, along with 75 wraps of cocaine and 32 wraps of heroin in the vehicle he was in.

Alan Ronald Ohara, 47, referred to as 'Rocket Ronny', was the driver, while 17-year-old Shane Walsh acted as Ali's lieutenant, responsible for preparing drugs for sale. Evidence presented in court indicated that Walsh had been involved in drug dealing since he was 16, and had continued his activities even after being released on bail.

The court heard that messages on Ohara's phone suggested he was involved in the management of the operation and was considering starting his own drug line. The prosecution highlighted the exploitation of Walsh, who had faced personal challenges and was groomed into the drug culture. Prosecutor Craig MacGregor noted that the gang had previously engaged in serious criminal activities, including bribing witnesses and using violence.

articles.title: Rochdale Police Launch Knife Amnesty Scheme
articles.excerpt: Rochdale police have introduced a knife amnesty scheme, allowing residents to anonymously dispose of knives and bladed weapons at designated bins across the district.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale police have launched a "Forever Amnesty" scheme, enabling residents to safely and anonymously dispose of knives and bladed weapons. The initiative features 13 permanent amnesty bins located across ten local districts, with three bins specifically situated in the Rochdale district.

The scheme aims to reduce knife crime and promote community safety by providing a secure method for individuals to surrender dangerous items without fear of prosecution.

Residents can find the amnesty bins at various locations throughout Rochdale, encouraging participation from the community to help create a safer environment.

This initiative is part of a broader effort by local authorities to address concerns surrounding knife crime and to foster a culture of safety within the community.

articles.title: Andy Burnham Calls for Deportation of Rochdale Grooming Gang Leader
articles.excerpt: Andy Burnham has vowed to take action to deport Shabir Ahmed, the leader of the Rochdale grooming gang, following his release from prison after serving 14 years for multiple rapes and sexual offences.
articles.content_html:
A man called Shabir Ahmed, the leader of a grooming gang in Rochdale, was released from prison earlier this month after serving 14 years for multiple rapes and sexual offences against young girls. Ahmed, who was born in Pakistan, was stripped of his British citizenship as part of his sentence and has since renounced his Pakistani citizenship, leaving him stateless.

In response to Ahmed's release, Andy Burnham, the MP for Makerfield, stated, "Like everyone, I want this vile criminal out of the country." He has urged the home and foreign secretaries to explore all options for deporting Ahmed, emphasising that victims must come first. Burnham's comments come as he prepares for his anticipated role as prime minister.

The current home secretary, Shabana Mahmood, has indicated she will seek to amend the Immigration Act 1971 to facilitate Ahmed's deportation. However, there are significant challenges ahead, as Pakistan has reportedly refused to accept him back, complicating the deportation process. The Pakistani government has previously stated that it would only accept the deportation of Ahmed if Britain extradited certain Pakistani dissidents, which has been deemed unacceptable.

Burnham's commitment to this issue may lead to diplomatic tensions, as Britain could consider applying pressure on Pakistan through measures such as cancelling visas or halting foreign aid. The situation remains fluid as discussions continue regarding the deportation of Ahmed and other members of his gang, Qari Abdul Rauf and Adil Khan, who were also released from prison and have renounced their Pakistani nationality.

articles.title: Man arrested on suspicion of attempted rape in Rochdale parks
articles.excerpt: A man in his 20s has been arrested on suspicion of attempted rape after two separate incidents in Rochdale parks this morning.
articles.content_html:
A man has been arrested in connection with two sex attacks in Rochdale. The man, in his 20s, has been held on suspicion of attempted rape following incidents that occurred less than two hours apart on Saturday, July 25.

The first incident took place in Broadfield Park at around 6:15am, where a woman reported being sexually assaulted by a stranger. The second incident occurred in Milnrow Memorial Park, reported at 8:38am, where another woman also claimed she had been attacked by an unknown man.

Greater Manchester Police (GMP) stated that both women provided similar descriptions of the suspect, who is described as a black male believed to have been wearing a three-piece suit or smart black clothing and a dark coat. He was also reported to have been carrying a briefcase. Police confirmed that a robust investigation is underway, and CCTV enquiries indicated a suspect leaving the Coco Lounge in Rochdale town centre at 5am.

In an update issued later, GMP confirmed the arrest of the man on suspicion of two counts of attempted rape. He remains in custody for questioning as enquiries continue. The victims are being supported by specialist officers during this time. Anyone with information is urged to contact GMP on 101, quoting incident numbers 79 and 880 of 25/07/2026, or to reach out to Crimestoppers anonymously.

articles.title: Police cordon in Rochdale town centre amid serious incident
articles.excerpt: A large area in Rochdale town centre has been cordoned off by police following reports of a serious incident, with unconfirmed reports suggesting a stabbing may have occurred.
articles.content_html:
A large area in the centre of Rochdale has been cordoned off amid a reported serious incident. Police have taped off the area between The Butts Avenue and South Parade on Thursday evening, July 23.

Pictures from the scene show several police vehicles present and officers standing guard at the cordon. The nature of the incident has not yet been confirmed by authorities.

There are unconfirmed reports from locals and social media suggesting that there has been a stabbing. Greater Manchester Police have been contacted for comment but have not yet responded to requests for a statement.

Anyone with information can find Greater Manchester Police and Crimestoppers contact details at the end of this article.
